---
title: "From h5ad files to L-cross functions"
author: "Valerio Reffo"
format: html
---

```{r}
#| label: development
#| include: FALSE

library(testthat)
```

This pipeline reads the cells of a slide and its tissue mask, builds a point
pattern, reduces the number of cells and estimates the L-cross function
between two cell types (here neoplastic and stromal cells).

The code runs on the example data shipped with the package.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(SpaFun)
library(spatstat.geom)
library(spatstat.explore)
```

## Reading a slide

`ann2ppp()` reads the h5ad file and uses the PNG mask as window. The masks are
thumbnails at 1.25x and the coordinates are at 40x, so each mask pixel is
40 / 1.25 = 32 coordinate units.

We read the small example file shipped with the package (it holds only a
small square of a slide, while the mask covers the whole slide):

```{r}
#| label: read-example

f    <- system.file("extdata", "tcga_tiny.h5ad", package = "SpaFun")
mask <- system.file("extdata", "tcga_tiny_mask.png", package = "SpaFun")

if (requireNamespace("anndataR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  pp_tiny <- ann2ppp(f, mask = mask, magnif = 40, marks_col = "type")
  print(pp_tiny)
  print(table(marks(pp_tiny)))
}
```

For the next steps we use a larger example: a crop of a slide with all its
cells, from `tcga_crops`.

```{r}
#| label: example-crop

data(tcga_crops)
pp_object <- tcga_crops[[1]]
table(marks(pp_object))
```

## Downsampling

Whole slides have up to millions of cells. We keep only neoplastic and
stromal cells and reduce each type separately with uniform thinning, which
leaves the L-cross function unchanged (see the "Downsampling" vignette).

On the example crop:

```{r}
#| label: downsampling

set.seed(10)
ppp_sub <- downsample(pp_object, method = "uniform", n_target = 5000,
                      marks = c("neoplastic", "stromal"), by_marks = TRUE)
attr(ppp_sub, "downsample")$n_kept_by_mark
```

## L-cross function

```{r}
#| label: lcross
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

r_values <- seq(0, 150, length.out = 70)

Lcross_neoStroma <- Lcross(
  ppp_sub,
  i = "neoplastic",
  j = "stromal",
  r = r_values,
  correction = "border"
)

plot(Lcross_neoStroma, . - r ~ r, main = "L-cross neoplastic - stromal")
```

## Several slides

For the functional analysis we need one curve per slide, all on the same
`r` grid, in a table with the column `r_value` and one column per slide
(the input of the "FDA pipeline" vignette). `downsample()` accepts a list of
patterns and processes them in parallel if a `future::plan()` is set.

```{r}
#| label: lcross-many

set.seed(10)
subs <- downsample(tcga_crops, method = "uniform", n_target = 5000,
                   marks = c("neoplastic", "stromal"), by_marks = TRUE)

L_list <- lapply(subs, function(x) {
  Lcross(x, i = "neoplastic", j = "stromal", r = r_values,
         correction = "border")$border
})

Lcross_table <- data.frame(r_value = r_values, L_list, check.names = FALSE)
head(Lcross_table[, 1:4])
```
